subject: linear predictor at the mesh nodes

messages.author: 6123b161185c6a93
messages.subject: linear predictor at the mesh nodes
parts:
Hi all,

I would like to make sure that my understanding regarding how to compute the linear predictor at the mesh nodes using inla.posterior.sample() is correct. I have checked all the questions on this topic in the forum but I have still doubts.
Let's say I have the following model:

log(y) ~ intercept + (beta1 + b1)*x1 + (beta2 + b2)*x2 + xi

model.formula = 0 + intercept + x1 + x2 + f(factor1, x1, model = iid) + f(factor2, x2, model = iid) + f(spde.index, model = spde.model)

model = inla(model.formula,......, control.compute = list(config = T),......)

sim1 <- inla.posterior.sample(n = 1, result = model)

ids <- lapply(c("intercept", "spde.index"),
function(x) grep(x, row.names(sim1[[1]]$latent), fixed = TRUE))

pred.f <- function(s) exp(s$latent[ids[[1]], 1] + $latent[ids[[2]], 1] + )

sim1000 <- inla.posterior.sample(1000, model)
pred <- sapply(sim1000, pred.f)

My question is: should I include the rest of the linear predictor terms (fixed effects, etc) in pred.f or just the intercept and the spatial random effect in order to obtain predicted values of the response at the mesh nodes?

Thank very much in advance
Juanmi
